source_acquisition.search_note: PDF 首页明确链接作者仓库 aiha-lab/ReQAT；inventory 的自动候选 NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer 与本文有关联但不是作者论文仓库。已核查作者仓库默认分支 main、commit 55038ae6ac807a33f9192a25a03f54a03789d21e 的 README 与递归 tree，并读取 Q-FIT、SEM、throughput 和 trackio 文件。仓库包含核心实现与一个通用 matplotlib 监控 notebook，却没有 Figure 1–11 或 Table 1–17 的精确 plot/table generator、TeX/TikZ 或导出数据；因此记录为 partial_visual_source。inventory 仍写 no_public_source_found，本轮仅在审计结果中反映作者链接，不改 inventory。

paper_style.palette_strategy: 定量图以灰、蓝、红、绿、紫等离散颜色区分 BF16、PTQ、QAT 与 ReQAT 阶段；机制图用低/高熵和路径色，Q-FIT 热图用蓝–红发散色，表格主要依赖黑白、粗体和星号。颜色、直接标签、行组和线型提供部分冗余，但大量渲染估计色值没有公开源文件支持。
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: 论文外壳文字和表格为 PDF 字体对象；Figure 1–11 为嵌入图形/栅格与矢量文字的混合视觉对象，Figure 8–9 尤其偏 raster/text trace；未发现可复用的精确导出源。
paper_style.style_consistency: 双栏 Letter 页面、caption 置于对象下方、Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern 数学字体和 booktabs 风格横线保持一致；复合图内部的字号、色彩和轴语法随对象职责变化，附录小图和宽表的密度明显更高。

encodings.y: accuracy drop or AIME accuracy (%) in (a-c); accuracy (%) in (d)
encodings.shape: bars in (a,c), point/line series in (b), scatter points in (d)

encodings.facet: four panels labelled (a)-(d) with distinct comparison grammars

figures.data_and_statistics: Panel (a) groups GSM8K, MATH-500 and AIME-120 accuracy drops after NVFP4 PTQ for Llama-8B, Qwen-14B, Qwen-32B and Llama-70B. Panel (b) plots AIME accuracy over 0–1.1B tokens for BF16, PTQ, Full-FT, Full-FT+PTQ, QAT, QAD and ReQAT. Panel (c) compares W4A4KV4 recovery variants. Panel (d) places accuracy against throughput speedup and annotates 3.1×, +9.1% and −65% storage; all are point estimates with no uncertainty or replicate summary.
figures.evidence_relation: Introduction identifies FP4 reasoning degradation → Figure 1 links the degradation, training-budget recovery and deployment trade-off → Tables 1–3 provide the exact budget/method values, while Figure 6 expands the throughput/memory claim.
design_strengths: Four panels move from failure magnitude to training recovery and deployment cost in one page-width object.
Panel (b) makes budget saturation and ReQAT’s trajectory visible; direct annotations in (d) make the headline trade-off scannable.
Repeated method names and bit-precision labels let the panels be read independently.
design_weaknesses: The four panels use unrelated scales and grammars, so cross-panel magnitude comparisons require the caption and surrounding prose.
No error bars or seed aggregation appear even though Appendix D.1 states eight random seeds; the accuracy–throughput panel has no uncertainty or Pareto-front explanation.
Small method labels and the multiple W4A4KV4 abbreviations are difficult at two-column reduction; direct storage/speedup callouts lack a denominator in the figure.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a four-panel evidence ladder—degradation, budget curve, recipe comparison, efficiency scatter—with repeated method colors and direct headline labels, while stating the evaluation unit and uncertainty once in the caption.

caption.text: Figure 3. ReQAT overview. ReQAT performs BF16 FT, calibrates RoPE quantization parameters (s, m) to minimize attention logit error Δz, and applies Q-FIT initialization followed by trace-aligned QAT with SEM loss on a TAQ subset to obtain an FP4 ReQAT model.

color.semantic_mapping: Neutral and pastel blocks distinguish BF16 FT, Q-FIT calibration, TAQ/SEM and the FP4 output; arrows and component labels carry the process semantics.

encodings.y: lower calibration target and data-subset relation
encodings.shape: rounded process blocks, arrows, formula cards and small probability bars
encodings.line: directed arrows from BF16 model to FP4 ReQAT model
encodings.text: BF16 FT, Q-FIT, Δz, TAQ subset, SEM, FP4 and output 3.05×/+9.11% callouts

figures.data_and_statistics: Pipeline schematic: BF16 FT precedes Q-FIT calibration of paired RoPE scale/shift parameters, then trace-aligned QAT with SEM on a TAQ subset, producing an FP4 ReQAT model. The diagram also includes the attention-logit-error target Δz and output callouts 3.05× token/s and +9.11% AIME accuracy, without axes or uncertainty.
figures.evidence_relation: Method introduces Q-FIT, TAQ and SEM as coupled stages → Figure 3 is the method interface → Figure 5 visualizes Q-FIT calibration, Figure 7 tests TAQ’s gradient mechanism and Tables 4–5 isolate the stages.
design_strengths: The left-to-right pipeline exposes stage order, data-subset nesting and the calibration objective in one view.
Arrows, block colors and formula text redundantly encode the interface, making the method easy to locate while reading the equations.
The figure links the method to deployment-level output callouts rather than leaving efficiency disconnected.
design_weaknesses: The output callouts lack an explicit configuration/denominator inside the schematic; DGX Spark uses W4A4KV8 while B200 uses native W4A4KV4, which is explained later.
Many formulas and small labels are compressed into one composite, with no visual distinction between training evidence and illustrative design.
The caption claims the full pipeline but does not define the SEM weighting or trace-alignment relation.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a single pipeline with explicit stage boundaries, data subset notation and one objective card; attach deployment numbers to a separately identified benchmark condition.

figures.evidence_relation: Results claim that FP4 reduces serving cost without losing ReQAT accuracy → Figure 6 is the efficiency/capacity evidence → Table 1/3 establish accuracy, and Appendix D.3 specifies hardware, software, request count and memory-saturated batching.

figures.reusable_pattern: Show normalized speedup beside a component-level memory budget and mark the hardware/path exception in the same visual object or caption.

figures.label: Figure 9

caption.text: Figure 9. Qualitative examples of entropy-selective logit-noise perturbation. Injecting noise into low-entropy token predictions often introduces minor symbolic errors that cascade into incorrect final answers, whereas perturbations applied only to high-entropy token predictions typically preserve the final answer despite altering the surface form of the reasoning trace.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue/green/red/gray and neutral cells separate BF16/quantized routes, high/low entropy interventions and correct/incorrect answers; seed rows and boxed answers add non-color redundancy.

encodings.color: green correct-answer box versus red incorrect-answer box; row headers identify intervention
encodings.facet: baseline, high-entropy noise and low-entropy noise rows
encodings.text: reasoning trace, boxed answers 104/70, check/cross markers and intervention labels

figures.data_and_statistics: Three stacked qualitative traces compare a baseline, high-entropy noise and low-entropy noise condition. Baseline and high-entropy noise end with boxed answer 104 and a check; low-entropy noise ends with boxed answer 70 and a cross. The example has no sample denominator, score distribution or uncertainty encoding.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 2’s noise-sensitivity panel predicts that low-entropy perturbations matter → Figure 9 illustrates the symbolic-error cascade at trace level → Table 15 controls for sampling versus greedy decoding and Figure 7 tests the training-side mechanism.
design_strengths: Identical trace layout makes the intervention contrast immediately comparable.
The final answer boxes and check/cross markers give redundant semantic cues beyond prose color.
The example concretizes why a small local symbolic error can affect the final reasoning result.
design_weaknesses: Long monospaced traces are difficult to scan and reproduce at page width; the selected prompt and generation settings are not stated in the caption.
Anecdotal traces cannot establish frequency or effect size, yet the caption uses “often” and “typically.”
The color-coded final answer is not accompanied by an aggregate count or link to the quantitative noise curves.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use aligned trace rows for a local causal illustration, and connect each trace to a quantitative perturbation summary and explicit selection protocol.

figures.label: Figure 10

caption.text: Figure 10. (a) Layer-wise calibration behavior with Q-FIT. We visualize key-cache statistics before and after RoPE across multiple layers, together with the corresponding calibration error heatmaps. (b) Training loss comparison under different QAT settings. Using an E1M2 KV cache consistently results in lower training loss compared to TAQ, which adopts E2M1 by default. Incorporating Q-FIT further reduces the training loss relative to TAQ-only variants, indicating more stable and effective quantized training (Model: R1-Qwen-14B).

figures.label: Figure 11

caption.text: Figure 11. Effect of block rotation and Q-FIT in MXFP4 W4A4. (a) Activation magnitude before and after block rotation, showing a small number of extreme outlier channels. After block-wise Hadamard rotation, outliers are redistributed across channels. (b) Training loss comparison under different QAT settings. tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1. AIME accuracy comparison of quantization methods on R1-Qwen-14B. ★ marks the best accuracy per bit-precision.

tables.uncertainty: All cells are point accuracies; no SD/SE/CI or seed dispersion is printed. The star marks the best cell within each bit-precision group, while Appendix D.1 states that results are averaged over eight random seeds.
tables.data_and_statistics: Rows group BF16, MXFP4 W4A16, MXFP4 W4A4 and NVFP4 W4A4KV4; columns are method plus 140M/210M/280M/350M total fine-tuning tokens. ReQAT_T, ReQAT_TQ and ReQAT_TQS provide staged TAQ/Q-FIT/SEM comparisons; the main headline is 68.02 for MXFP4 W4A16 and 65.94 for MXFP4 W4A4 at 350M.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 1 introduces budget/recovery trajectories → Table 1 is the central budget-by-precision result surface → Table 2 transfers to R1-Llama-8B and Table 3 broadens the baseline set; Table 5 isolates Q-FIT components.
design_strengths: The four bit-precision groups keep accuracy and token budget in one decision surface.
Stars and bold values make within-group best results easy to locate.
The staged method names expose cumulative additions of TAQ, Q-FIT and SEM.
design_weaknesses: Twenty body rows and narrow single-column typography make method suffixes and budgets hard to scan.
The caption does not define T/TQ/TQS or repeat the eight-seed averaging rule; the main text supplies those definitions.
Point estimates and best-cell selection omit dispersion, so small differences across neighboring budgets lack visible evidential weight.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use grouped rows for precision and a fixed token-budget header for cumulative method ablations; define suffixes and replicate aggregation in the caption.

evidence.label: p.7 Table 1: headers, body, rules, highlighting, caption, and placement inspected from the 200 dpi render

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2. Results on R1-Llama-8B under NVFP4 W4A4KV4 (Total fine-tuning budget: 350M tokens) across various benchmarks.

tables.uncertainty: All GSM8K, MATH-500 and AIME-120 entries are point accuracies; no uncertainty or per-task sample count is reported, although Appendix D.1 states eight random seeds.
tables.data_and_statistics: The first two rows are BF16 baseline/FT; five NVFP4 W4A4KV4 rows compare Direct PTQ, FT+PTQ and ReQAT_T/ReQAT_TQ/ReQAT_TQS across three benchmark columns. AIME improves from 23.13 Direct PTQ to 41.85 ReQAT_TQS, while GSM8K/MATH-500 remain high.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 1 establishes the R1-Qwen-14B budget trend → Table 2 tests model transfer under a fixed 350M budget → Figure 6 and Table 7 test deployment/code-generation generalization.
design_strengths: The compact three-task header makes cross-benchmark transfer immediately visible.
The fixed total budget is stated in the caption, preventing a direct budget confound within this table.
Rows preserve the stagewise ReQAT decomposition used in Table 1.
design_weaknesses: The caption does not state dataset sizes or seed aggregation, so cross-task differences cannot be weighted.
Precision and method grouping is indicated through sparse cells, which can be missed at reduced scale.
No delta column or highlighted best cells makes the magnitude of recovery require manual subtraction.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a fixed-budget cross-task table with a shared method vocabulary and add explicit task denominators or uncertainty when comparing transfer claims.

evidence.label: p.7 Table 2: headers, body, rules, highlighting, caption, and placement inspected from the 200 dpi render

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3. Comparison with existing PTQ methods on AIME benchmark across different quantization settings (R1-Qwen-14B).

tables.uncertainty: AIME accuracies are point estimates with no variance display; rows combine full-precision, W4A16 and W4A4KV4 settings, so precision and method effects are identifiable only through the Bit-Precision/FT columns.
tables.data_and_statistics: Six columns encode bit precision, whether FT is used, method, format, group and AIME accuracy. The 16 body rows include BF16 baseline/FT, AWQ/QAD/QAT/ReQAT under W4A16, and QuaRot/FlatQuant/QAT/ReQAT under W4A4KV4; checkmarks in FT and sparse precision cells form row groups.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 1 supplies budget curves → Table 3 anchors ReQAT against PTQ/QAT baselines at matched settings → Table 4–5 explain why the method components recover accuracy.
design_strengths: Format and group-size columns make the hardware-relevant comparison more specific than method names alone.
Sparse checkmarks efficiently identify fine-tuned rows and bold highlights the strongest result.
The three row groups allow the reader to separate BF16 reference, W4A16 and end-to-end FP4.
design_weaknesses: The table is dense for a single column and the checkmark/sparse-cell convention is not defined in the caption.
Rows mix PTQ and FT variants with different transformation formats; no cost or runtime column accompanies the accuracy decision.
No uncertainty or matched-seed information appears, while the prose uses strong across-setting comparisons.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a compact baseline matrix with explicit precision, format and group-size columns, but pair it with a separate cost/uncertainty view.

evidence.label: p.7 Table 3: headers, body, rules, highlighting, caption, and placement inspected from the 200 dpi render

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4. Effect of two-stage QAT and trace alignment under different token budgets (MXFP4 W4A16 R1-Qwen-14B).

tables.uncertainty: Three rows report point AIME accuracies for four token budgets; no uncertainty or replicate values are shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: Columns are Method, Trace Aligned, and 140M/210M/280M/350M. QAT and FT+QAT without aligned traces are followed by FT+QAT with alignment; the final row reaches 67.29 at 350M and is bolded.
tables.evidence_relation: The TAQ mechanism claim in Figure 7 → Table 4 isolates trace alignment while holding MXFP4 W4A16 and R1-Qwen-14B fixed → Table 5 then isolates Q-FIT design choices.
design_strengths: One binary trace-alignment column makes the controlled factor explicit.
The common budget columns align directly with Table 1 and expose the late-budget gain.
Minimal booktabs rules preserve readability in a narrow column.
design_weaknesses: Only three rows and point estimates cannot show variation or interaction with trace composition.
The caption does not define how “Trace Aligned” is operationalized or how the two-stage budget is split.
The table has no delta column, so the “about 5%” conclusion is not directly displayed.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a one-factor ablation with a boolean treatment column and shared budgets; print the treatment delta and replicate summary when the claim is quantitative.

tables.label: Table 5

caption.text: Table 5. Ablation of Q-FIT designs (W4A4KV4 R1-Qwen-14B).

tables.uncertainty: Final loss is reported to four decimals and AIME accuracy to two decimals; all values are point estimates without SD/SE/CI.
tables.data_and_statistics: Six columns encode method, E1M2 KV, pre-RoPE scale, post-RoPE shift, final loss and AIME accuracy. Five rows cover ReQAT_T and ReQAT_TQ variants with checkmark/dash combinations; the full Q-FIT row is bold in accuracy and has the lowest loss (0.7633).
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 5 visualizes calibration geometry → Table 5 tests E1M2, pre-RoPE scale and post-RoPE shift combinations → Figure 10 and Table 17 provide layer-wise and rotation comparisons.
design_strengths: The binary component columns make Q-FIT’s joint design legible without repeating long method names.
Reporting loss beside AIME keeps optimization and task evidence on one ablation surface.
Mixed precision in the loss column is appropriate for distinguishing close optimization values.
design_weaknesses: Checkmark/dash semantics and row grouping are compact but not defined in the caption.
The final-loss comparison may be a training diagnostic rather than an independently validated endpoint; no training-step or seed context is included.
No uncertainty and no explicit direction arrows accompany the four-decimal loss values.
tables.reusable_pattern: Put component toggles beside both training and task outcomes, and state whether each outcome is seed-averaged and evaluated at a common checkpoint.

tables.label: Table 6

caption.text: Table 6. Accuracy across response-length ranges (AIME-120, W4A4KV4 R1-Qwen-14B). Each cell reports acc/#samples.

tables.uncertainty: Each cell explicitly reports accuracy/sample count as acc/#samples; the denominator varies by response-length bin and is useful context, but no seed or sampling uncertainty is shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: Rows compare BF16 baseline, BF16 FT, PTQ, FT+PTQ, QAT and ReQAT; columns split 0–8K, 8–16K, 16–24K and 24–32K responses. Values are percentages with one decimal and sample counts after a slash; ReQAT reaches 19.3/249 in the longest bin.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 6 addresses serving length/capacity → Table 6 tests reasoning accuracy as response length grows → Figure 9 illustrates a local cascade and Table 15 controls decoding strategy.
design_strengths: The acc/#samples notation makes the changing denominator visible instead of hiding long-response scarcity.
Length bins form a direct stress axis for the quantization-failure claim.
Rows include both full-precision and quantized baselines, anchoring the degradation.
design_weaknesses: The caption does not define whether bins overlap, how responses are sampled or how accuracy is aggregated across seeds.
Long-bin cells have small counts relative to short bins, yet the table gives no interval or stability cue.
The one-decimal accuracy format can imply more precision than the long-bin denominators support.
tables.reusable_pattern: Report outcome and denominator together for stratified stress tests, with a minimum-count or replicate cue when tail bins are sparse.

The stagewise TQ/TQS rows preserve the mechanism decomposition.

A single aggregate hides problem-type heterogeneity and uncertainty.
No best-cell emphasis or delta column makes the comparison less immediate than Table 1.

caption.text: Table 8. Quantization configurations of MXFP4 and NVFP4.

tables.uncertainty: This is configuration metadata rather than a performance estimate; uncertainty is not applicable.
tables.data_and_statistics: Two rows identify MXFP4 and NVFP4; five columns specify element data type, block scale data type, global scale data type and block size alongside the format name.

tables.label: Table 9

caption.text: Table 9. Accuracy drop Δ (AIME-120) under NVFP4 W4A4KV4 on R1-Llama-8B, measured relative to the corresponding full-precision FT baseline.

tables.uncertainty: Entries are point accuracy drops Δ in percentage points; no uncertainty or individual-seed drops are shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: The first header cell names FT/QAT epochs k and columns 1–5; two rows compare FT(k-ep)→PTQ with FT4-ep→QAT(k-ep). Drops are relative to the corresponding full-precision FT baseline, with the largest displayed values around 15.42 and 13.65.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 6 shows length-stratified failure → Table 9 tests whether extra epochs repair the drop → Table 13 compares multi-epoch TAQ with ReQAT, closing the “more training alone” alternative.
design_strengths: The delta-only format focuses attention on degradation rather than duplicating absolute scores.
Five epoch columns make the non-monotonic trend easy to scan.
The caption states the reference baseline and deployment setting.
design_weaknesses: The row label `FT4-ep` and arrow notation require surrounding prose to decode.
No absolute accuracy or replicate spread accompanies the drops, so practical significance is hard to assess.
The caption does not define whether k epochs reuse the same 70M-token subset or alter data exposure; that detail is elsewhere.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a delta table for a controlled stress axis only when the reference baseline and absolute companion result are explicitly linked.

evidence.label: p.18 Table 9: headers, body, rules, highlighting, caption, and placement inspected from the 200 dpi render

tables.label: Table 10

caption.text: Table 10. Year-wise AIME accuracy on R1-Qwen-14B under NVFP4 W4A4KV4. For fine-tuned methods, we report the best accuracy across training budgets.

tables.uncertainty: Year-wise values are point accuracies; no year-level uncertainty is shown. Fine-tuned rows report the best budget, creating a selection effect that the caption does disclose.
tables.data_and_statistics: Columns are method, AIME 2022/2023/2024/2025 and Avg. Nine rows include several BF16 reference variants, BF16 FT, PTQ, FT+PTQ, QAT and ReQAT; ReQAT has 67.92/65.42/71.25/59.17 and average 65.94.
tables.evidence_relation: Main results aggregate AIME-120 → Table 10 decomposes the aggregate by year and compares the reproduced AIME-2024 baseline to official/reported references → Table 1 retains the budget sweep.
design_strengths: The year-wise split exposes whether the aggregate gain is concentrated in one test year.
The Avg. column preserves direct linkage to headline AIME-120 values.
Official/reported baseline rows provide a provenance check for the reproduced evaluation.
design_weaknesses: “Best accuracy across training budgets” selects a maximum and can make fine-tuned rows optimistic relative to fixed-budget rows.
Several baseline provenance labels are long and crowd the single-column table.
No budget or seed dispersion is shown for the selected values, limiting comparability across methods.
tables.reusable_pattern: Decompose an aggregate benchmark by year and retain provenance rows, while reporting the budget-selection rule and selection uncertainty beside the table.

tables.label: Table 11

caption.text: Table 11. Key hyperparameters for training in our experiments.

tables.uncertainty: Hyperparameter metadata has no statistical uncertainty; the table is a deterministic configuration record.

It includes data, optimization, batching, checkpointing and precision rather than only the learning rate.
The two-column structure is easy to cite from code or experiment logs.

Long dataset and objective strings are dense at appendix size.

caption.text: Table 13. Multi-epoch TAQ vs. ReQAT on AIME (R1-Llama-8B).

tables.uncertainty: AIME accuracies are point estimates without uncertainty; the bold ReQAT 41.85 is the best displayed value.

tables.evidence_relation: Table 9 tests extra FT/QAT epochs → Table 13 compares multi-epoch TAQ with one-epoch ReQAT → Figure 7 and Table 4 explain why aligned, targeted learning differs from simply increasing exposure.

tables.label: Table 14

caption.text: Table 14. Results of ReQAT on MMLU benchmark (model: R1-Qwen-14B).

tables.uncertainty: AIME-120 and MMLU values are point accuracies with no uncertainty or task-count metadata.
tables.data_and_statistics: Four columns list Bit-Precision, Method, AIME-120 and MMLU. Six body rows group BF16 baseline/FT, W4A16 MXFP4 PTQ/ReQAT and W4A4KV4 NVFP4 PTQ/ReQAT; precision is sparse across grouped rows.

tables.label: Table 15

caption.text: Table 15. Accuracy (AIME-120) under NVFP4 W4A4KV4 on R1-Llama-8B, measured relative to the corresponding full-precision FT baseline. T denotes temperature.

tables.uncertainty: Rows report point accuracies and derived Δ values; no seed dispersion is shown. Δ is explicitly the difference FT−FT+PTQ within each decoding setting.
tables.data_and_statistics: An eight-column, two-level header separates Sampling (T=0.6, top-p=0.95) and Greedy (T=0, top-k=1), each with FT, FT+PTQ and Δ over FT epochs 1–5. Sampling drops are 11.05–15.42; greedy drops are 7.50–15.00.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 2 diagnoses token-level noise → Table 15 controls decoding strategy as an alternative source of failure → Figure 9 illustrates the local trace effect, and Table 9 tests epoch scaling.
design_strengths: The two-level header makes sampling parameters and method rows explicit.
Derived delta rows expose the quantization penalty without forcing mental subtraction.
Five epoch columns reveal that lower greedy drops coexist with lower absolute accuracy.
design_weaknesses: The page-width table is dense and requires horizontal scanning across eight columns.
The caption defines T but not the generation seed/count, so accuracy and delta stability are unclear.
Comparing sampling and greedy changes both stochasticity and absolute baseline, so the causal interpretation needs the surrounding paragraph.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use paired decoding blocks with explicit parameter headers and within-block deltas, while retaining the absolute baseline needed to interpret mitigation versus performance loss.

tables.label: Table 16

caption.text: Table 16. Ablation results of λ in SEM (R1-Llama-8B).

tables.uncertainty: GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME-120 and Avg. are point accuracies; bold marks the best average (74.11) with no uncertainty.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: 视觉叙事从 Figure 1 的 FP4 degradation/budget/recovery/throughput headline，经 Figure 2 的低熵 token 机制诊断，进入 Figure 3–5 的 TAQ、SEM、Q-FIT 方法接口，再由 Figure 6–7 连接部署成本与梯度机制；附录 Figure 8–11 和 Tables 8–17 扩展路由案例、trace 噪声、layer calibration、rotation、配置、年度切片、超参与消融边界。
cross_object_system.caption_system: Figure caption 统一采用对象标题加 panel 说明；机制和附录 caption 会写出方向性结论，主结果 caption 多为设置/比较标签。caption 很少定义误差、重复、分母和缩写，T/TQ/TQS 等语义主要留给正文。
cross_object_system.table_header_system: 表头主要用 Bit-Precision/Method、token budget、benchmark 和 deployment format 组合；booktabs/minimal 横线与稀疏 row group 保持外壳一致。多级表头见 Tables 1、13、15、17，且多数表只给点估计，不带 uncertainty 列。
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 3 建立 BF16 FT→Q-FIT→TAQ+SEM 的流程，Figure 4/5 与 Tables 4/5/12/16/17 分别将 entropy、trace alignment、Q-FIT、SEM 和 rotation 变成可检验消融；Tables 1–3、6–7 把组件组合映射到准确率/泛化。
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: 正文 Figure 5 指向 Appendix Figure 10，正文 Figure 2 的 routing/noise 诊断由 Figures 8–9 具象化；正文 Tables 1–7 的配置、年度分解、epoch、解码策略、MMLU 和 λ/rotation 消融由 Tables 8–17 补齐。
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: 正文 caption 与表格的 PDF 字体对象稳定为 Nimbus Roman No9 L 配合 Computer Modern 数学；图内标签多为 4–9 pt 的渲染估计，Figure 9 的 trace 使用等宽字。附录复合图的内部字号变小，但未出现跨对象字体家族断裂。
cross_object_system.color_consistency: 灰色常承担 BF16/reference，蓝/绿/红/紫承担量化或 ReQAT stage，低/高熵和 Q-FIT heatmap 有局部语义；表格主要用黑白粗体/星号。直接标签、panel、row group 和 checkmark 提供冗余，但图内红色警示与多色小图在灰度和缩印下辨识度下降。

most_reusable_patterns: Figure 1 把 degradation、training-budget recovery 和 accuracy–throughput trade-off 排成一个证据阶梯，适合把机制论文的 headline 与部署代价放在同一阅读路径。
Figure 2 将直觉 token 示例、分布扰动、routing policy、noise sensitivity 和 tail/mismatch 组合成从现象到机制的诊断链。
Figure 3 的阶段化 pipeline 与 Tables 4–5 的二值组件消融形成方法接口—结果对照，读者可以追踪 TAQ、Q-FIT、SEM 的增量。
Table 6 的 acc/#samples 和 Table 10 的 year-wise breakdown 展示了把分母/切片显式放进结果对象的可复用做法。
Appendix Figure 10/11 与 Tables 8、11、15–17 将 layer、quantization metadata、hyperparameters、decoding 和 alternative transformation 作为复现边界补齐。
